prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A weekly class timetable for quick lookup of when a lesson occurs, what subject it is, who teaches it, where it meets, and any notes.","reading":"Read right-to-left: scan the merged day blocks first, then the time within each day, then read across subject → teacher → room; notes are secondary and consulted only after the lesson row is identified.","groups":["Columns 1–2 (day + time) form the schedule anchor and should stay adjacent and dominant.","Columns 3–5 (subject + teacher + room) form the lesson identity and should read as a compact row unit.","Column 6 (notes) is ancillary and should not compete with the schedule or lesson columns."],"keep_intact":["Day names","Time ranges, ideally unbroken","Subject names without mid-word splits","Teacher names, allowing wraps between words","Room identifiers where possible"],"may_wrap":["Notes text, freely","Teacher names between words","Long subject words only when forced","Room labels only when forced"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [62, 82, 64, 52, 44, 55] · table 360×3453px · row heights [60, 478, 478, 455, 432, 478, 385, 687] · column headers wrapped 3/6 · tallest cell 29 lines · mid-word splits 70
Design r0B: widths [62, 110, 84, 89, 97, 100] · table 543×1663px · row heights [36, 246, 222, 199, 199, 246, 176, 339] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 14 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 183px
Design r0C: widths [62, 110, 95, 85, 80, 180] · table 613×779px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 253px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
